reasons: Thorough coverage of the Desk in Hindi, but no run result is visible here.

terms.meaning: the language and regional settings that control how text and numbers are shown
a page marker that tells browsers and screen readers which language the page is in

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Hindi switch and persistence
sections.what: Switches the Desk and navigation to Hindi, checks the translated labels, text, sources and language marker, confirms the choice survives a reload, and switches back.
sections.why: Verifies the translation end to end, including the saved preference.
sections.watch_out: The expected Hindi strings are exact, so any translation edit will break this test.

summary: Browser test that switches the Desk and navigation to Hindi with the language toggle, checks the text and layout, confirms the choice is saved, and switches back.
purpose: Confirms the Hindi translation works across the Desk, including numbers, labels and sources, and that the setting persists.
why: Users who read Hindi need the whole Desk translated, and a choice that resets on reload would be frustrating.
how: It opens the Desk in English, clicks the language toggle, and checks the heading, navigation link, swing and provisional labels, depth text, receipt region and pending section all switch to Hindi. It confirms the page language attribute changes. It reloads to confirm Hindi is still selected, runs an accessibility check, and toggles back to English.
inputs: The Desk page and its first item.
outputs: Pass or fail for translation, persistence and accessibility.
risks: Expected Hindi wording is hard-coded, so any change to translations breaks the test.
debug: Compare the failing string with the translation file. If the reload check fails, look at how the language choice is stored.
